rules.header_subtitle: Learn how the setup works, how turns progress, what the Executioner does, and how to win.
rules.step1_title: Step 1: Setting up Decks & Initial Cards
rules.step1_desc: Organize the first row by placing the Black Market (BM) deck on the left, line up the Plot Armor (PA) cards face up in the center by color (Intelligence, Wisdom , Dexterity , and Strength ) — note that their number equals the total number of players, e.g., if there are 2 players, there will be 2 Strength PA, 2 Intelligence PA, 2 Dexterity PA, and 2 Wisdom PA and excess PA cards are removed from the game — and place the Executioner's deck on the far right.
rules.step2_desc: Directly below the first row, set up the Death Line by placing the Executioner below the Black Market(BM) deck.
rules.step2_list1: The Executioner: Always takes the very first position on the far left.
rules.step2_list2: The Peasants: Place all Peasant cards immediately after the Executioner. They act as protection for the players.
rules.step2_list3: Character Selection: All players choose a character that represents them for the game. Any unpicked characters are removed from the game. Shuffle the chosen Character cards and pick one at random to decide who starts first in the queue behind the Peasants.
rules.step2_list4: Seat Arrangement: Place the remaining player characters in order, following the natural seating order around the table in a clockwise direction. Players' positions in the Death Line are important: Players always draw and play cards in the order dictated by the Death Line. Additionally, if all other players die, the last living player automatically wins the game. Players can sometimes change positions in the Death line, but only amongst themselves. Players cannot swap positions with peasants.
rules.step2_list5: Main Deck & Discard Pile: After the end of the Death Line, place the Main Deck (MD).Unless stated otherwise, all cards are drawn from the MD. Make sure to leave space near the MD for the Discard Pile. All used cards are sent to the Discard Pile face up.
rules.step3_desc: Directly below the Death Line, create the Board by drawing cards from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.step3_list1: Number of Cards on Board: Deal a number of cards equal to the number of players + 2 onto the board.
rules.step3_list2: Card Types: The board contains 2 types of cards: Resource cards (Red Cardback) and Action cards (Blue Cardback). Resource Cards are always placed face up and Action Cards are always placed face down on the Board. Note - if Black Market(BM) Cards are shuffled into the MD, they count as Action Cards and are placed face down.
rules.step4_list3: Starting Hand: At the start of the game, each player draws 3 cards from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.phase1_desc: The game officially begins with the Draw Phase, the first of three phases of each round.
rules.phase1_list1: Turn Order: Players choose and draw cards from the board strictly in the order they appear in the Death Line.
rules.phase1_list3: Empty Board Rule: If there are no available cards on the board, players draw directly from the Main Deck (MD).
rules.phase1_complete_desc: Drawing continues along the Death Line until every player has chosen one card from the board. Once every player has picked and drawn a card, the Draw phase ends.
rules.phase1_complete_list2: Board Reduction: As players take cards, the board will naturally shrink, giving players further back in the Death Line fewer options.
rules.phase2_desc1: After the end of the Draw Phase, the Action Phase begins. Always according to the order dictated by the Death Line, players can do one of the following:
rules.phase2_opt1: 1) Play an Action or Black Market(BM) Card: Play a blue action card or a Black Market(BM) card from your hand, immediately apply its effect, and then send it to the Discard Pile.
rules.phase2_opt2: 2) Purchase a Plot Armor (PA) Card: Discard 3 identical Resource cards + 1 Holy Duck Tape card from your hand to claim an available corresponding Plot Armor card. Claimed PA cards are placed in front of the player, with their text face up. Each color of PA cards has a unique effect that can be activated once per round, that counts as a free action (meaning the player does not lose their priority in the action phase). Note: The Plot Armor card does NOT go to the Discard Pile when you use its effect; it stays in front of the player.
rules.phase2_opt3: 3) Purchase a Black Market (BM) Card: Discard any 3 cards from your hand to take the top card from the Black Market(BM) deck. This counts as a free action, meaning you can purchase a Black Market(BM) card and immediately decide to do any of the other main actions, without passing priority.
rules.phase2_opt4: 4) Pass : Pass priority to the next player in the Death Line.
rules.phase2_priority_title: Priority & Passing in the Action Phase
rules.phase2_priority_text1: During the Action Phase, each player takes one action on their turn, or they can choose to pass and do nothing. The order of priority is defined by the Death Line. Once the last player of the Death Line has finished their action, priority passes back to the first player of the Death Line, until all players consecutively have chosen to pass. If any player makes an action other than passing, priority carries to the next player as per normal. Once all players have passed, Action Phase ends.
rules.phase2_ex1_title: Example of Playing an Action Card
rules.phase2_ex1_text: The active player plays Unfair Trade to execute its effect ("Draw 2 cards from the Main Deck"). Afterwards, the card goes to the Discard Pile as shown in the image below. The next player in the Death Line takes priority.
rules.phase2_ex2_title: Example of Purchasing a Plot Armor Card
rules.phase2_ex2_text: To purchase a Strength Plot Armor card, discard 3 Strength Resource cards along with 1 Holy Duck Tape card.
rules.phase3_desc: After the end of the Action Phase, the Executioner's Phase begins. During this phase, the players are passive and the Executioner dictates the course of the game: Reveal the top card of the Executioner's Deck and immediately resolve its effect. Used Executioner's cards are placed in a seperate deck nearby. When the Executioner's deck runs out of cards, reshuffle the used Executioner's card back to its original deck and continue the Executioner's Phase as per normal.
rules.phase3_list1: Refilling the Board: The board is refilled only when the Executioner decides to give you a chance, instead of killing someone. When the board is refilled, existing cards are not sent to the descard pile. Instead, empty slots are filled with cards from the Main Deck (MD), never exceeding the number of players + 2.
rules.phase3_list2: YOU ARE UP NEXT: When this card is revealed, the Executioner executes the very next card in the Death Line. The board isn't refilled
rules.phase3_list3: Peasant Protection: The Executioner must first execute all Peasants before any player is in danger.
rules.phase3_list4: Flipping to Death State: When a player character dies, flip their card to reveal the Death State artwork. The player is removed from the game. Similarly, when a peasant dies, flip their card to reveal their Death State Artwork (peasants can sometimes be brought back to life, again serving as protection for remaining players).
rules.phase3_list5: End of the Executioner's phase: Once the effect of the next card on the Executioner's card has been resolved and there are more than 1 players remaining, the round is over. The game continues by looping back to the draw phase.
rules.phase3_ex1_text: Drawing "YOU ARE UP NEXT" executes the next card in the Death line.
rules.phase3_ex2_text: Executed characters flip over to reveal their Death State.
rules.purpose_text1: Prove that you are the protagonist! The first player to collect 3 Plot Armor cards wins.
rules.purpose_text2: Alternatively, if all other players die, the last survivor wins immediately.

executioner.name: The Executioner
executioner.description: Beauty is both a blessing and a curse. That's the problem of our beloved Executioner. Legends say his first conquest was the midwife who delivered him. Having spent his entire life as the embodiment of the halo effect, he grew tired. What's the point when everything and everyone comes so easily? So, he did the only thing that made sense: he decided he is a fighter, not a lover. He took over the family business and became the new Executioner. Associated with death itself, surely people would stop looking at him just for his looks. And with endless grace and sex appeal, even in this, he finally succeeded. Now he is not just a handsome guy. He is the sexy Executioner.

notferatu.name: Notferatu
notferatu.description: He is a ruthless and relentless vampire hunter. After his mother died when a vampire that cursed her blood (-she suffered form sepsis), he vowed to dedicate his life to becoming the greatest vampire hunter in the world, so no one else would ever go through what he did. After years of training and finding the perfect equipment, he is finally ready to face a vampire... once he finds one. His latest trick? Dressing up as a vampire himself so that a real one would come out of hiding without fear... and then... then... the local villagers mistook him for a vampire and sent him to be executed. He is now waving garlic around, scubbbing off his makeup, and shouting that he is a human hoping to saved himself. En vain, though, since everyone already knows he is human, they just wanted an excuse to get rid of him after 10 long years driving everyone crazy with his vampire obsession.

misero.name: Misero
misero.description: Humor ages with man. We don't know if that's true, but that is the state of the king's once-beloved clown. After more than 40 years of jokes, cream pies and sarcasm, this clown stopped spreading smiles and joy. In a last attempt to become funny again, he decided to reinvent himself by changing his stage name from Bozo to Smiley, Harley King, Sad Sad Sammy, and every other terrible name imaginable, until he finally gave up and called himself Misero. Now, all he wants is to retire. But the king won't let him because, besides being useless enterntainment, he also happen to be the king's only real advisor (when you're the clown who no one pays attention to, you over hear a lot). Finally, he decided to go out the way he lived: with a joke. He made a particularly vulgar one about the queen's behind and ended up in line for execution. He is oddly happy about it, until a child gives him a clown scepter and says he is his biggest fan. Realizing he can still make someone laugh, Misero decides... it's not his time yet.

paprika.name: Paprika
paprika.description: A young maid with a talent for cooking who, despite being barely able to read, finds a spice book with pictures and uses it for her next pie. She leaves everyone speechless as they've just tasted the most gourmet medieval dish imaginable. A woman who's good at something, can read, and uses spices? She must be a witch! The court sentenced her to two months of community service, but she requested execution because she is in love with the Executioner (she thinks she can "fix" him). After annoying the judge for over 3 hours, he gave up and sentenced her to death. Unfortunately, while waiting in the execution line, she suddenly remembered that if the Executioner kills her, she will never see him again! So, she decided to escape and change her approach.

hamlet.name: Hamlet
hamlet.description: It's the Middle Ages. A pig appears out of nowhere, knocks a flowerpot off a lady's balcony, and it falls on the head of the local lord, killing him instantly. Would you call that man slaughter or murder? Whether it's a pig doesn't matter... someone must pay for this tragic accident. The worst part? The pig actually is intelligent and self aware. In fact, he is a secret member and informant of an underground organization plotting against the regime. His plan all along was to assassinate the noble so that the city would fall into the control of this secret order and all without breaking the law! After all, who would accuse a pig? Well, everyone actually, because he forgot he's in the Middle Ages when people do believe animals have consciousness and criminal law is still in its early stage and so a cunning conspirator now finds himself desperately trying not to become bacon.
